entries.title: Jeremiah 44:1
segments: Migdol; on the north-eastern frontier of Egypt towards Palestine.
; a large city of ancient Egypt on the west bank of the Nile, a little above Cairo.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:2
segments:
vv 2-10. 
 
When wicked men refuse to take warning from the punishment of those who have practised the same sins before them, it is a great aggravation of their guilt.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:9
segments: Have ye forgotten the wickedness--in the land of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem?  have ye forgotten the judgments which I brought upon you for your wickedness there?

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:11
segments:
vv 11-14. 
 
God's wrath follows the wicked into every place whither they flee for safety, and overthrows all their vain confidences.  It is only by repenting and returning to him that they can escape destruction.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:15
segments: Their wives had burned incense; their wives were leaders in idolatry.  Probably some of them were of heathen origin.  Compare

. 
 
vv 15-23. 
 
Wicked men are prone to impute their misfortunes to every other cause, rather than the true one; nay, more, to seek a return of prosperity from those very practices which have brought ruin upon them.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:24
segments:
vv 24-30. 
 
They who will no longer hear reproof are in the road to speedy destruction; God will fight against them and their helpers, and both shall perish together.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:26
segments: Shall no more be named in the month of any man of Judah; because all shall be destroyed except a small remnant.

entries.title: Jeremiah 44:30
segments: Pharaoh-hophra; the reigning monarch of Egypt, called "Apries" by the Greeks.  He was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish, and afterwards dethroned and strangled by his own troops.
